fields.depends_on: Artifact dependencies. A ticket enters the ready queue when each is ENGINEERING_COMPLETE, DONE, DEFERRED or BLOCKED_EXTERNAL. While one is BLOCKED_EXTERNAL this ticket closes only as ENGINEERING_COMPLETE (records carry inherited_block).
fields.needs_decision: Decision dependencies (D-x in DECISIONS.md). Work proceeds on the recorded default labelled ASSUMED; never capped; re-validated if the answer differs.
fields.required_evidence: Set of distinct Stark v9.3.0 levels; DONE needs one evidence record per listed level.
fields.slices: Single-PR slices of at most 10 h. Required before IN_PROGRESS for any ticket over 12 h.
fields.validation_hours: Opus validation budget (separate session from the implementer).
fields.external_blocker: {owner (role, never a guessed person), unblock_step, needed_by, raised_on}; days waiting = today - raised_on while unresolved.
fields.due: Hard date for gate tickets; other tickets follow their wave window in PLAN.md.

tickets.title: Establish the release evidence chain and readiness labels (ADR-017) and make the ledger reject closure without evidence
tickets.summary: False closure is the program's biggest risk (ChatGPT audit section 5): persuasive reports and green unit tests are not packaged-product proof. Define one immutable evidence record per level per ticket linking requirement or defect, reproduction, commit, artifact hash, environment, executed test, result, implementer and validator, and a checker that computes closure from those records. It also fixes the dependency rule: artifact dependencies cap closure, decision dependencies do not (work proceeds on the recorded default, labelled ASSUMED).
acceptance: JSON schema for evidence records: ticket, evidence_level, per-kit_ref status (MET/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/NOT_MET), finding_refs, repro, commit, artifact_sha256 (packaged), environment and host identity, command, exit_code, result, ci_run_id, implementer_session, validator_session, inherited_block; one record file per ticket under docs/metis-2.0/evidence/records/

Status vocabulary TODO/IN_PROGRESS/ENGINEERING_COMPLETE/BLOCKED_EXTERNAL/DEFERRED/DONE/CANCELLED documented in docs/metis-2.0/README.md; DEFERRED means shipped flag-off with a recorded owner approval under the degrade order (D-14)

Dependency semantics in the README: depends_on lists artifact dependencies; a ticket enters the ready queue when each is ENGINEERING_COMPLETE, DONE, DEFERRED or BLOCKED_EXTERNAL; while an artifact dependency is BLOCKED_EXTERNAL the downstream ticket can close only as ENGINEERING_COMPLETE, its records carry inherited_block, and it becomes DONE when the upstream is DONE and the affected verification is re-run. needs_decision lists D-x decisions: work proceeds on the recorded default labelled ASSUMED, is never capped by the decision, and is re-validated if the recorded answer differs (the check lists those tickets)

required_evidence is a set of Stark v9.3.0 levels, which are distinct and unordered (DESIGNED, LOCALLY_TESTED, HOST_CONFIGURED, LIVE_VERIFIED, ACCEPTED, MEASURED); scripts/evidence/check.mjs requires one record per listed level before DONE and rejects any other level value

LOCALLY_TESTED needs a CI run ID on the PR head SHA; LIVE_VERIFIED needs harness-produced suite or census output plus the artifact sha256 from the build lane (M2-0187) and the host identity, never prose; MEASURED needs the raw measurement file; ACCEPTED needs the owner's dated statement
Fix tickets carry red-before (the new test fails on the parent commit) and green-after runs, both recorded

'Wired for real' is defined and checked: a real client code path with no production stub, a schema-faithful contract fake used only in tests, a one-command live probe script, and BLOCKED with the unblock step visible in the in-app capability matrix; anything less is NOT_MET
implementer_session must differ from validator_session (a reviewer never approves its own work); the PR template requires the evidence record path and the reviewing model
check.mjs refuses IN_PROGRESS for a ticket over 12 h without slices of at most 10 h
scripts/evidence/sample.mjs draws a random 10% of tickets closed since the previous gate for re-execution by a different model; results are recorded as evidence with reexecuted_by

Exception by definition of done: the program sign-off (M2-0184) may be DONE with inherited blocks, because the goal defines done as engineering-complete with every external dependency BLOCKED and visible; its record lists each inherited block with its unblock step

tickets.title: Stop foreign-key and keystore failures from quarantining the brain index: ownership stamp plus decrypt-failure taxonomy
tickets.summary: quarantineUnusableIndex renames any index.json that fails to decrypt, so a process holding a different key (a test worker, another device on a shared .brain) resets the owner's ledger and forces a full re-ingest, which feeds the heavy-machine loop. Stamp a plaintext index.owner.json with the existing installId on every successful writeIndex, and classify decrypt failures as unparseable, foreign-key or keystore-unavailable. Only an unparseable index owned by this install (or unowned, for backward compatibility) is quarantined; everything else stays byte-identical and opens read-only for the session.
acceptance: writeIndex stamps .brain/index.owner.json {installId, updatedAt} (no content) after each successful write
Foreign installId or keystore-unavailable leaves index.json byte-identical, returns an in-memory empty read-only index and audits brain.ledger.foreign_key (content-free)
Own or unowned plus unparseable keeps today's rename behaviour; new quarantine snapshots are capped at 5; the existing 180 index.corrupt-* files are never deleted by the app
Correlation note records quarantine timestamps against known test-run windows (metadata only, owner-approved) to close CRITIC-INV-2
Three ownership cases plus the backward-compatible case are covered in mqa-175-brain-index-poison.test.ts

When the ledger opens read-only (foreign-key or keystore-unavailable), the index is flagged unavailable so the scheduler suspends backfill, ingest, consolidation and the intelligence catch-up (deferredReason ledger_unavailable) instead of re-extracting every meeting against the empty in-memory index; data health shows the state

Two-device case: a .brain shared by two installs flips the owner stamp; a test proves neither device quarantines or re-ingests, and the remaining risk is stated as a 1.9.7 residual until the ledger moves to userData (M2-0205)

tickets.title: Make model choice an Operator-managed fleet policy: the owner picks models per capability in the portal and every Métis app enforces it
tickets.summary: Owner requirement (2026-09-28, OD-18): 'I decide what model on the portal and every Métis app abides by that.' Today model choice is local: each app reads its own settings (src/shared/ipc.ts BaseSettingsSchema provider default 'cloudflare') plus an optional admin-managed config file (src/main/store.ts allowedProviders, readTrustedAdminManaged). The Operator portal brokers asks (operatorAskTransport in src/main/import-recap.ts) and has settings-store / seat routes, but there is no portal page that sets models and no fleet policy the apps fetch and obey. The Operator serves the policy as a signed, versioned document on a device-authenticated endpoint (use the existing seat / desktop-license device authentication now; switch to M2-0145's per-device HMAC binding when it lands). Every app verifies the signature before use; a tampered or unsigned policy is rejected with an audit event.

Electron app (macOS + Windows) and native Mac app fetch the policy at start and on change (push or poll <= 60 s), cache the last valid signed policy for offline use, and route every model call through it — the local settings cannot select a model outside the policy (Settings shows the policy's choice as managed/locked with the portal as the source).
Operator-brokered calls enforce the same policy server-side: a request naming a model the policy does not allow is refused (typed error), so an old or modified client cannot bypass it.
Precedence is defined and tested: owner portal policy > MDM admin-managed file allowedProviders (can only narrow) > user settings; no policy yet = today's defaults with a visible 'not managed' state.

Tests: Operator route + signature tests (vitest), desktop policy client tests (fetch, verify, cache, offline, change applied without restart), a contract test that every model call site resolves through the policy module, native Mac unit tests (Swift, CI), and a packaged-smoke row POLICY-01 on macOS + Windows: change the policy on a test Operator, the running app switches model within 60 s.

tickets.title: Add automated WCAG AA contrast and clipping audits to the design-capture lane, with an in-Electron negative control and a pull_request trigger on design paths
tickets.summary: M2-0101 acceptance 4 needs automated WCAG AA contrast and clipping checks on captures from the real Electron renderer. The M2-0418 lane (PR #309, head c3834a87, open and mergeable) has none. scripts/design/* has no contrast, clipping or WCAG code (triage basis). capture-states.mjs only screenshots and hashes, and manifest entries carry only state, theme, scale, motion, file and sha256 (capture-manifest.mjs buildManifest). design-capture.yml is workflow_dispatch only (line 15; 'On demand only' at line 11) and is not registered on main yet. Its upload-artifact step (line 52) has no if: always(), so a failing run would upload nothing. Under D-28, the design PRs that follow (M2-0450, M2-0451) have no way to prove their states pass before merge. The reference standard is the one the superseded HTML-mock audit applied (private docs/metis-2.0/evidence/M2-0101/design/audit.json 'standard'): WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.3 text contrast (4.5:1, large text 3:1); 1.4.11 non-text contrast of controls and the focus indicator (3:1); and no clipped text, horizontal scroll or content outside the window. That audit ran in the private prototype, which the public repo cannot use, so this ticket reimplements it, self-contained, in the public capture lane. It is the first of three gap tickets for M2-0101 (then M2-0450 and M2-0451). Placement W3/m5 matches M2-0418 and M2-0101.
acceptance: A pure module scripts/design/capture-audit.mjs computes WCAG relative luminance and contrast ratio. It alpha-composites the element colour over its resolved background, walking up the ancestors' backgrounds. Thresholds: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text (>= 24 px, or >= 18.66 px at weight >= 700), and 3:1 non-text (1.4.11) for control boundaries (button, input, select, switch and checkbox borders or fills against the adjacent background) and for the focus indicator. Unit tests cover #000 on #fff = 21:1, #767676 on #fff passing 4.5:1, #777777 on #fff failing it, a 50%-alpha text colour composited correctly, and the large-text boundary

Clipping checks: a visible text-bearing element fails when scrollWidth > clientWidth + 1 or scrollHeight > clientHeight + 1 while overflow is hidden or clip or text-overflow is ellipsis. The page fails when documentElement.scrollWidth exceeds the viewport width, and any visible element whose box extends horizontally outside the viewport fails. The predicates are pure and unit-tested on synthetic box data

An in-page collector runs in the Electron renderer for every captured shot. Each manifest entry gains audit {pass, text {checked, failures}, nonText {checked, failures}, clipping {checked, failures}, unverifiable}. The manifest gains a top-level audit summary {standard, failures, per-kind check counts, negativeControl}. Failure rows are content-free: tag or role, a short selector, measured and required ratio, and the two colours, never text content

Vacuity guard: a state with zero text checks or zero clipping checks fails as a 'vacuous audit'. Text over a background that cannot be resolved (gradient or image) is listed as unverifiable and counted in the summary, never as a pass

Negative control: a QA-only state audit-negative-control is resolvable by ?state= but is not in DESIGN_STATE_IDS and is never written as evidence. It renders one low-contrast text, one low-contrast control boundary and one clipped label. The driver audits it first, in both themes, and exits non-zero unless all three are detected. The manifest records negativeControl.detected=true with the detected kinds
When any evidence state fails, the job still writes manifest.json and uploads the artifact (upload step if: always()), then exits non-zero

design-capture.yml also runs on pull_request to m2/integration when src/renderer/src/design-capture/**, scripts/design/** or the workflow file change. It keeps workflow_dispatch and gets no push or tag trigger, permissions stay contents: read, no secrets are used, and every uses: stays SHA-pinned (check:workflow-pins passes). The header comment is updated to match

No new npm dependency. The existing M2-0418 tests are updated, not deleted (the manifest-entry test gains the audit field). The M2-0418 placeholder states pass the audit on both OSes, or this PR fixes their capture.css tokens

tickets.title: Find and fix why the packaged app on hosted macOS usually never starts its bundled model for the HK-M model rows, and report the start failure at once instead of a silent 240 s BLOCKED
tickets.summary: M2-0028's LIVE_VERIFIED check (HK-M 20/20) cannot pass today. In 7 of the last 9 m2/integration packaged smokes on macos-latest, the model-starting and active-inference rows end BLOCKED_EXTERNAL scenario_not_triggered. The blocked runs are 36555124400, 36558892407, 36562304816, 36580907773, 36593670201, 36601733280 and 36613722413; the two passes are 36551144543 (5f0197ff) and 36572749687 (980cfe10). Compare the pass run 36572749687 with the blocked runs 36613722413 (6ea79002) and 36601733280 (51132486). In the blocked rows the registry has no intent and no spawned record (pass: intent 1, spawned 1). There is no local.runtime.start, sidecar.spawn is 1 instead of 2, and no llama-server process appears, so the app never reached local-runtime's spawn. Each blocked row then waits the full 240 s SCENARIO_TIMEOUT_MS (19:09:34 -> 19:13:37 -> 19:17:41 in 36613722413), and the macOS job takes 29.5-31 min instead of 16 min. All three runs used the same runner image (macos-26-arm64 20260907.0351.1) and the same runtime-assets cache key, and check:local-model verified the same bundled qwen3.5-0.8b hashes (model.gguf 558772480 bytes 3177ebd6..., mmproj.gguf 204987232 bytes). The rows' unblock text ('confirm the bundled local model is packaged and intact') is therefore wrong. Pass and block alternate across unrelated commits. The pass runs reach renderer-ready in about 1.0-1.3 s, while the blocked runs take 1.5-3.8 s. This points at the host, not the code (DERIVED). The reason is thrown away: qa-hooks.ts routes a row's setup error to mainLog.warn in the throwaway profile, and hk-m.mjs deletes that profile (removeTempDir). Leading hypothesis (DERIVED, unverified): ensureLocalRuntimeStarted calls verifyIntegrity, and its assertRamOk throws InsufficientRamError before any registry intent when advertisedRamGB() = ceil(totalmem/GiB) is below qwen3.5-0.8b's minTotalRamGB of 8. That happens on a runner VM that exposes exactly 7 GiB; a host exposing slightly more rounds up to 8 and passes. A missing llama-server candidate (local.runtime.missing) would also leave no intent. M2-0430 is not the likely cause. Its os.freemem() reading only chooses the GPU or CPU profile in spawnProfileFor, after the start decision, and a runner below GPU_OFFLOAD_MIN_RAM_GB (12) gets the CPU profile regardless. The other freemem floor (PREWARM_MIN_FREE_RAM_GB 4 in local-routing.ts) gates only speculative prewarm, and the HK-M hook bypasses it by calling ensureLocalRuntimeStarted without canStartSpeculatively. So this ticket does not depend on M2-0430. The override this ticket may add stays inside the HK-M hook, so on its own it does not unblock the scenarios that start the model through window.toto.localPrewarm (M2-0467, M2-0468 realLlama, M2-0470 control). The evidence line below settles whether they need a follow-up. Separately, hk-m-candidate.yml is on main at df205007, but GET actions/workflows/hk-m-candidate.yml returns 404 (not registered), and qa-candidate.yml has never been dispatched. Triage: codex-queue/logs/ec-triage-result-2026-09-29.json (M2-0028).

acceptance: New .github/workflows/candidate-scenarios.yml, triggered by workflow_dispatch only. Inputs: candidate_run (required); scenario (a choice; this PR adds fault-fatal-relaunch); mac_sha256 and win_sha256. The resolver requires the sha256 inputs the chosen scenario needs and rejects any it does not use. run-name shows the scenario and candidate_run. Permissions are contents: read and actions: read, the workflow uses no secrets, and every uses: is pinned by full SHA (check:workflow-pins green).

A guard job on ubuntu-latest runs only for this repository and only on refs/heads/main, using the same repository and ref guard as qa-candidate.yml. It refuses any candidate_run that is not a completed, successful workflow_dispatch run of .github/workflows/qa-candidate.yml on main, so pull-request self-test candidates are refused. A pure function in scripts/qa/candidate-scenarios.mjs makes this decision from the Actions API run JSON, and it has unit tests.

scripts/qa/candidate-scenarios.mjs holds a scenario registry that is the single source of truth. For each scenario it declares the platforms, the qa-candidate variant and artifact to install, the command and the report file. fault-fatal-relaunch installs mac-qa-identity (the Metis-QA zip). Scenarios that need no QA-only hook install the promotable mac or win variant, so their records bind to promotable bytes. The contract test asserts that the workflow's scenario choices equal the registry keys.

The mac job downloads candidate-provenance and the scenario's artifact from candidate_run, runs provenance.mjs verify, and asserts that provenance.run.id equals candidate_run. It picks the installer whose sha256 equals mac_sha256 using scripts/qa/candidate-installer.mjs (from M2-0416), extended to *.dmg and *.zip; a mismatch or a missing file fails the job with no fallback. It installs into a fresh directory under RUNNER_TEMP (DMG via hdiutil and ditto, zip via ditto -x -k) and passes codesign --verify --deep --strict. The lane never builds the app; npm ci runs only so that the scenario scripts' imports (for example playwright-core) resolve.

Fresh profile: for the QA identity the job asserts that the QA userData directory does not exist before the run. It then seeds only the settings the scenario declares; for fault-fatal-relaunch that is the localLlm block that sidecar-boot-reaper.mjs seedLocalLlmSettings writes (enabled, qwen3.5-0.8b), so the prewarm can start the bundled model.

The fault-fatal-relaunch step runs `node scripts/qa/fault-fatal-relaunch.mjs --zip <QA zip> --sha256 <mac_sha256> --out <report>`. Exit codes map to outcomes: 0 is PASS, 1 is FAIL and 2 is PRECONDITION. The job fails on anything but PASS, but only after the upload step.

Every run uploads (if: always()) a content-free artifact named candidate-scenario-<scenario>-<platform>. It holds the scenario report plus lane.json with: schema, scenario, platform, runner label with ImageOS and ImageVersion, build_run_id (= candidate_run), commit (from provenance), variant, installer file name, artifact_sha256, ci_run_id (this run), environment {kind: 'hosted-runner', host: 'macos-latest'}, command (repo-relative, no absolute path), exit_code and outcome. The field names match the evidence-record fields, so the lead can copy them straight into a LIVE_VERIFIED record (M2-0466).

Content-free gate before upload: every file to be uploaded is scanned for a user-home path (/Users/<x>, /home/<x>, C:\Users\<x>), an email address and the runner account name. A hit fails the job and the offending file is not uploaded. Each pattern has a unit test.
The job summary prints the lane.json fields and the outcome. A PRECONDITION outcome is annotated with the script's precondition text (::warning) and never reads as PASS.

It never isolates the legacy rule: 'legacy-orphan' is only accepted as an alternative reapedReason (:122). That rule (acceptance[2]; src/main/infra/process/reaper.ts ~174-200) matches only a llama-server that runs the bundle's llama-server binary, has ppid 1, started before the current main, and has a -m argument under <userData>/local-llm; it never matches by name alone. The row needs a harness-spawned orphan that points at a pinned-model copy seeded into the profile, which is what the triage's 'seed the pinned local model into the fresh profile' means. tickets.title: Build the on-device speech-pack engine in new files behind a default-off flag: pinned per-file manifest, verified resumable download, atomic activation
tickets.summary: Owner request 2026-09-29: speech models (Whisper, Parakeet) download during onboarding. This is the part that can land before the 1.9.7 soak. It is new files only, imported by nothing outside its folder, with the flag off by default, so the 1.9.7 candidate bytes and every file 1.9.7 fixed stay unchanged (PD-12 not triggered). It keeps the ordering guarantees of src/main/asr-model-download.ts (whole-transfer disk check; .partial files renamed only after length and sha256 match) and the redirect and HTML guards in src/shared/bundle-response.ts. It adds byte-range resume and a staged, self-tested atomic activation. Components: asr.whisper-base-q8 and asr.parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8. OD-30 (owner, 2026-09-29): onboarding downloads the on-device speech engine selected for this machine automatically — visible card with engine, size, free disk and host, live progress, Skip — never blocking Continue/Finish; the other engine stays an optional download in Settings.
acceptance: manifest.ts pins asr.whisper-base-q8 (11 files, 81,263,214 B) and asr.parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8 (encoder, decoder, joiner, tokens.txt; 670,478,772 B). Bytes and sha256 must match resources/runtime-assets-manifest.json exactly, and a unit test fails on any difference.

Every source URL is immutable: pinned to a commit per file, never a branch such as main (the never-main rule from asr-model-manifest.test.ts applies). If Parakeet has no per-file pinned upstream, the upstream archive is pinned by its own byte count and sha256. Each extracted file is then checked against its per-file pin, and extraction is capped for size and guarded against path traversal. The M2-0162 R2 route can later become the first source without changing any pin.

Before the first byte, free space is checked for the remaining bytes plus the extraction peak plus 512 MB of headroom. A shortfall returns error kind 'disk' with the required and free bytes, and nothing is written.

Each file streams to <name>.partial and resumes with an HTTP Range request guarded by If-Range. A 200 reply or a changed validator restarts only that file. A file is renamed only after its length and sha256 match. On a mismatch the partial file is deleted and the file is retried once from zero, then the error is 'tamper'. HTML or login-page responses report 'captive'. Timeouts are 60 s per request and 120 s idle. Retry-After is honoured with capped exponential backoff and jitter. A file that already passed verification is never downloaded again.

Activation: all files are verified in a staging directory, then an injected self-test must decode the pinned 184,608-byte en.wav fixture to non-empty text, then one atomic rename moves them to userData/speech-packs/<component>/<version>, with an active.json marker written last. Tests that kill the process at every step show a crash never leaves an active marker or a half-filled active directory.

State per component, with no user content: not-installed, queued, downloading{bytesDone, bytesTotal}, verifying, self-testing, ready, paused, or error{offline|disk|tamper|captive|http|cancelled}. Only one download per component at a time. Cancel and pause work. The selected engine is queued first. Events are sent at most once every 250 ms. No transcript, audio or user text appears in any state or log.

Flag speech-pack: --speech-pack=on|off on the command line or METIS_SPEECH_PACK=on|off (the command line wins), off by default, following src/main/infra/process/supervisor.ts. A contract test proves that no file outside src/main/features/components/speech-pack/ imports the module in this ticket.

Vitest runs in CI only (D-28) against a local HTTP fixture server and covers: a cut at 30% then a Range resume; a server that ignores Range; one flipped byte; a captive HTML page; offline; a disk shortfall; cancel; and kill points during activation.

tickets.summary: Waits for the soak under PD-12. index.ts, ipc.ts and listen.ts were edited by 1.9.7 tickets (M2-0429, M2-0036, M2-0026 and others), and parakeet.ts by the packaged-smoke fix c2d20122. OD-30 (owner, 2026-09-29): onboarding downloads the on-device speech engine selected for this machine automatically — visible card with engine, size, free disk and host, live progress, Skip — never blocking Continue/Finish; the other engine stays an optional download in Settings.
acceptance: With the flag on, resolveParakeetDir, resolveWhisperModelsRoot and the asr-model:// handler (through its existing userModelsRoot) use the active, verified pack. Bundled resources still win whenever present (1.x and the M2-0372 full offline profile), and a damaged bundle is still never masked by a copy in userData.
On a lean profile, a missing pack reports PACK_NOT_INSTALLED or PACK_DOWNLOADING with bytes, never 'Repair or reinstall'. That message remains only for a full profile whose bundled files are damaged.

IPC adds speechPack:state, speechPack:start(components), speechPack:cancel and speechPack:retry, plus a pushed speechPack:progress event (no user content, throttled), all typed in preload. The renderer never polls faster than once per second.
A pack chosen by the user or by policy resumes in the background after the first window is shown and never blocks start-up. The ST-1 budgets (M2-0433) are unaffected; all I/O is async.

If the selected engine is still downloading when a capture starts, the capture shows 'On-device transcription is downloading: 410 of 670 MB. Transcription starts automatically when it finishes.' It starts transcribing on the ready event without restarting the capture. The silent Parakeet-to-Whisper switch in listen.ts (console.warn only) is replaced by this visible state. If the other engine is ready, the user is offered one click: 'Use Whisper base until then'.
During a capture, a download that capture is waiting on continues. Any other pack download pauses and resumes afterwards (kit §14.7).
The launch-time check reads the marker and file sizes only, with no re-hashing on each launch (as M2-0035 did for local models). The full sha256 check runs at activation and on Repair.
Vitest covers the resolver, the IPC contract and the listen state changes, in CI only. A contract test proves behaviour is unchanged with the flag off against today's packaged paths.

With supervision on (M2-0483), the wrapper's argv is 'metis-mac-helper supervise --parent <pid> -- <bundle>/.../llama-server ...' (supervisor.ts wrapperArgs). Every census or soak sample with a model running would therefore report two llama-server processes and add the wrapper's footprint to that role. The 1.9.7-versus-1.9.6 comparison (acc 4a after) would show a spurious doubling of the llama-server count, and the OD-35 by-role growth rule would be keyed on a wrong population (DERIVED from the code). HK-M and the reaper harness classify by executable basename (owned-processes.mjs), so they are unaffected. fault-fatal-relaunch.mjs classify has the same path match, but it only tests presence and strays, so the error there is harmless and is left to M2-0467. This is harness-only, so it can land after the cut, but it must land before the census and soak runs on the candidate. [Lands after the cut; runs on the candidate's bytes.]
acceptance: classifyProcess returns 'sidecar-supervisor' for a process whose executable basename is metis-mac-helper and whose first argument is 'supervise'. That check runs before the llama-server and fm-serve matches. Other metis-mac-helper processes keep today's classification
'sidecar-supervisor' is added to ATTRIBUTABLE_PROCESS_KINDS and reported as its own kind. On a supervised sample, the llama-server count equals the real runtime count

lib.test.ts fixtures pin these cases: a wrapper around llama-server gives sidecar-supervisor; a wrapper around fm serve gives sidecar-supervisor; a bare bundled llama-server gives llama-server; Windows rows are unchanged; a non-supervise metis-mac-helper process is unchanged
Reports stay content-free: sanitizeReport is unchanged, and no command line or path enters the report
CI Build & Test is green

tickets.title: Census long-run mode: stream samples to NDJSON as they are taken, count job and sidecar audit events from the profile's audit trail, and sample Windows private bytes
tickets.summary: The M2-0009 census tool keeps every sample in memory and writes one JSON only when the run ends (collectCensus, scripts/qa/census/lib.mjs:595-651; identical on origin/main df205007 and origin/m2/integration 761276bc). If a 5.5 h hosted leg hits the job limit or the app dies, that leaves nothing. The tool also counts no jobs. M2-0046 acc 4 requires 'no unbounded growth in processes or jobs'. Without a product change, the only job signal a hosted run can read is the isolated profile's audit trail: userData/logs/audit.log plus the audit-<stamp>.log generations (logger.ts:53, AUDIT_ARCHIVE_PATTERN :408). Each line is {ts, seq, prev, event, ...}, with scheduler.job, brain.ingest, brain.backfill.start, sidecar.spawn/exit, local.runtime.* and mcp.push.* events. On Windows the tool samples only Win32_Process.WorkingSetSize (WIN32_RESOURCE_QUERY). The OS trims the working set, so a heap leak can hide in it; PrivatePageCount does not. This ticket adds an opt-in long-run mode for the OD-35 idle soak (M2-0492/S7) and the meeting run (M2-0496). The default 300 s report (schemaVersion 1) stays unchanged, so M2-0200 can still reuse the tool as-is. CUT TIMING: scripts only (no installer bytes, no qa-candidate.yml), so it can land AFTER the cut. [Lands after the cut; runs on the candidate's bytes.]
acceptance: run.mjs --ndjson <path> first writes a header line: schema 'census-stream/1', state, platform, productVersion, mainPid, intervalMs, startedAt and profileKind. It then appends one line per sample and flushes it immediately: tMs; per process pid, startedMs, kind, rssBytes, physFootprintBytes, workingSetBytes, privateBytes and cpuSeconds; mainAlive; sampleDurationMs. A trailer line is written only on a normal end. A unit test stops a fake collector after N samples, then parses the file with no trailer.
When the main pid is gone, the sample records mainAlive:false. The run then ends with trailer outcome 'main-exited' and does not keep sampling an empty population. A unit test covers this.

--interval-ms is a period: each sample is scheduled from the previous sample's start. Every line records sampleDurationMs, so slow vmmap or CIM calls are visible. A fake-clock unit test covers the schedule.

Windows samples add privateBytes from Win32_Process.PrivatePageCount, taken in the same CIM query; on macOS privateBytes is null. sanitizeProcessSample gains the field as an additive change, and lib.test.ts expectations are updated. schemaVersion 1 is otherwise unchanged.

scripts/qa/census/audit-counts.mjs <userData> --from <iso> --bucket-minutes <n> --out <json> reads the rotated audit-<stamp>.log generations in order, then audit.log, and tolerates a torn last line. Per bucket it counts only this allowlist: scheduler.job by its outcome enum, brain.ingest, brain.backfill.start, brain.consolidation, brain.intelligencePass.start, brain.intelligence_index, mcp.push.queued, mcp.push.retried, local.runtime.start/stop/crash/restart, sidecar.spawn, sidecar.exit, sidecar.reaped, app.stall, history.request, plus a single 'other' count.
audit-counts never copies actor, detail fields, file names or text into its output. A fixture trail that carries detail and actor fields proves that only event names, enum outcomes and counts leave.

run.mjs --audit-counts <out.json> (used together with --ndjson) refreshes the counts every --checkpoint-minutes (default 10) and at the end. A run that is killed still leaves counts up to its last checkpoint.
Without the new flags, the output of `run.mjs --state settled-idle --seconds 300` keeps today's key set. A unit test compares the sanitized report keys before and after.
resource-census.yml is not changed in this PR. Build & Test is green. CI only (D-28).
verification: CI Build & Test

tickets.title: Growth analyzer with pre-registered rules IDLE-GROWTH-1 (idle leg, extrapolated to 8 h) and MEETING-GROWTH-1 (1 h meeting), frozen by a pinned hash before any data exists
tickets.summary: OD-35 judges each hosted idle leg (macOS and Windows, at most 5.5 h each) by a growth rule pre-registered before the run and extrapolated to 8 h. M2-0046 acc 4c needs the same kind of judgement for the meeting hour. No analyzer exists. The rule is written into the file before any real data arrives, following the M2-0479 pattern, and a contract test pins its hash, so any later edit is a visible, reviewed change. The analyzer reads M2-0487's NDJSON and audit counts and judges process count by kind, respawns, memory slope and step, CPU drift and job-event rate. It reports INCOMPLETE rather than PASS on short or gappy data. Kinds are the census kinds, including 'sidecar-supervisor' (M2-0486): with supervision default-on (M2-0483), every supervised runtime brings one wrapper, and the rules allow the wrapper wherever they allow its runtime. The defaults below are the pre-registration draft, and the lead may amend them (including the validity margin inside a 330-min leg) only before the LEAD_ACTION registration. CUT TIMING: scripts only, so it CAN LAND AFTER THE CUT, but it must be merged and registered before the first idle-soak or meeting-history dispatch. [Lands after the cut; runs on the candidate's bytes.]
acceptance: growth-rule.mjs exports frozen RULES.IDLE_GROWTH_1 and RULES.MEETING_GROWTH_1. Its header states every clause in prose. Default constants: 30 s sampling; 20 min idle settle (meeting: the first 5 min of capture); 10-min buckets, each valued at the median of the per-sample totals. Kinds are the census kinds, including sidecar-supervisor

IDLE-GROWTH-1 P1: for every process kind, no bucket median is above that kind's count in the last settle bucket. P2: distinct process identities (pid + start time) per kind are at most the settle count + 2, and audit sidecar.spawn in the window is at most 2. A sidecar-supervisor wrapper counts with, and is allowed alongside, the runtime it supervises

IDLE-GROWTH-1 M1: take the Theil-Sen slope of the bucket medians of total memory (macOS phys_footprint sum, Windows private-bytes sum) and project it to 8 h after launch. Projected growth from the end of settle must be at most max(64 MiB, 10% of the settle-end total); per kind the limit is max(32 MiB, 15%). M2: the last bucket minus the first window bucket stays within the same bounds

IDLE-GROWTH-1 C1: mean one-core CPU% over the last 60 min is at most the first 60 min after settle + 0.5 points. J1: allowlisted job events in the last 60 min are at most the first 60 min + 3, and no bucket has more than 20. Validity: at least 300 min measured after settle, at least 95% of planned samples, and main alive at every sample. A main exit is FAIL, not INCOMPLETE

MEETING-GROWTH-1 applies P1/P2 over capture minutes 5-60. ASR, speaker, llama-server and one sidecar-supervisor wrapper per supervised runtime may appear before minute 5. Post-meeting per-kind counts are at most the capture counts, with +1 llama-server and +1 sidecar-supervisor allowed for the summary. M1 over the capture hour: renderer at most max(96 MiB, 25%), because the live transcript lives in renderer state until the m5 journal; total at most max(160 MiB, 20%); other kinds (including sidecar-supervisor) at most max(32 MiB, 15%). The post-meeting end total is at most the minute-5 total plus the total bound. J1: no capture bucket has more than 20 job events. Validity: at least 55 min of capture and at least 95% of samples

growth.mjs --samples <ndjson> --audit-counts <json> --rule <id> --out <verdict.json> writes: outcome PASS|FAIL|INCOMPLETE; each check's measured value, bound and pass flag; the projected-to-8 h values (idle rule); the rule id and the sha256 of growth-rule.mjs; the sha256 of each input file; and the residual 'linear extrapolation cannot see a leak that starts after the leg ends'. It never reports PASS with a failed or missing check. Exit codes: 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 INCOMPLETE

growth.test.ts fixtures: a flat idle leg (PASS); a flat idle leg with llama-server and its wrapper present from settle (PASS); a linear leak within bounds at 5.5 h but over them at 8 h (FAIL by projection); step growth (FAIL M2); a respawn loop (FAIL P2); rising CPU (FAIL C1); a job storm (FAIL J1); a 4 h leg (INCOMPLETE); a main exit (FAIL); a meeting with renderer transcript growth within bounds (PASS); a supervised summary start after Stop, llama-server plus wrapper (PASS); an ASR utility leaked after Stop (FAIL)
growth-rule.contract.test.ts pins the sha256 of the serialized RULES. Any change fails CI until a reviewed PR updates the pin and states why
Output is content-free (numbers, kinds, event names). Build & Test is green. CI only (D-28)

LEAD_ACTION, before the first idle-soak or meeting-history dispatch: record both rule ids, the pinned sha256 and the merged commit in the private release-1.9.7 evidence folder (a growth-rule registration note) and in M2-0046's notes. A verdict whose rule sha256 differs from the registered one is not valid evidence
verification: CI Build & Test

tickets.title: resource-census.yml measures a qa-candidate run's exact bytes: candidate_run + mac_sha256/win_sha256 inputs, plus a report-only per-state delta against the 1.9.6 baseline run that refuses model-confounded comparisons
tickets.summary: resource-census.yml accepts only release_repo and release_tag, so no census can bind to the candidate sha256 before promotion. Under OD-31 the before/after comparison must be in front of the owner when he records ACCEPTED, so measuring the promoted tag afterwards is not enough. This ticket adds a candidate source to the same workflow, so every measurement step (install, footprint, profile, TTFT, states) stays identical and baseline and candidate share one method. For installing candidate bytes it reuses M2-0467's run guard (scripts/qa/candidate-scenarios.mjs) and the sha256 selector (scripts/qa/candidate-installer.mjs, M2-0416/M2-0467). Candidate legs launch exactly like the release legs, without M2-0482's floor override, because the 1.9.6 baseline cannot set it. The model may still start on one side only (1.9.6's freemem prewarm floor against the candidate's available-memory floor), so the delta records llama-server presence and marks a state NOT_COMPARABLE where it differs. The per-kind delta uses M2-0486's classification, so the supervised candidate's wrapper appears as the new sidecar-supervisor kind rather than doubling llama-server. M2-0200's gating compare.mjs depends on M2-0046 and comes later; this ticket adds only a report-only delta. CUT TIMING: workflow and scripts only, so it CAN LAND AFTER THE CUT. The run takes about 80 min after the cut and must finish before ACCEPTED. [Lands after the cut; runs on the candidate's bytes.]
acceptance: New optional inputs: candidate_run, mac_sha256, win_sha256 and baseline_run. On each leg a resolver step accepts exactly one source. 'release' (release_tag) is today's behaviour and the default. 'candidate' needs candidate_run plus that leg's sha256. Any other combination fails before any download, and run-name shows the source

Candidate source: the pure guard from scripts/qa/candidate-scenarios.mjs refuses any run that is not a completed, successful workflow_dispatch of qa-candidate.yml on main. The leg downloads candidate-provenance and candidate-mac (DMG) or candidate-win (Setup), runs provenance.mjs verify, and asserts provenance.run.id == candidate_run. It selects the installer whose sha256 equals the input through candidate-installer.mjs; a mismatch fails with no fallback

The selected installer is staged where today's install step reads it. Install, footprint, both profiles, TTFT and every census state then run unchanged. Candidate legs never set METIS_QA_HOST_FLOOR_OVERRIDE, and run-identity.json records hostFloorOverride false and the host memory
Permissions are contents: read and actions: read. No secrets are used. Every uses: stays SHA-pinned (check:workflow-pins green), and the main-ref guard stays

run-identity.json gains source, build_run_id, commit (from the provenance), artifact file name and artifact_sha256. Artifacts keep today's os tokens: resource-census-macos|windows-<release_tag | candidate-<run>>

With baseline_run, each leg downloads that run's census artifact for its OS and runs scripts/qa/census/delta.mjs for each state present in both runs (cold-start, settled-idle, parked-idle). It reports deltas of CPU-seconds per 300 s, the phys_footprint sum (macOS) or the working-set and private-bytes sums (Windows), and process count by kind

delta.mjs marks a pair NOT_COMPARABLE when the profile-manifest sha256, state list, seconds or interval differ. A kind present only on the candidate (sidecar-supervisor) is listed as a new kind, not as a regression. It never fails the job on a regression; thresholds belong to M2-0200. The delta JSON and a job-summary table are uploaded

tickets.title: ST-1 on the candidate with synthetic dataless fixtures (profile-shaped, History idle, 5 min), a stated real-dataless row and the packaged stat-flags local rows, in qa-candidate.yml (OD-36)
tickets.summary: OD-36 moves ST-1 on real evicted cloud files to the owner's 5-day soak (M2-0198), and the candidate itself must carry ST-1 with synthetic dataless fixtures. M2-0031's row ('a dataless .brain/index.json with no History interaction, 5 min from launch') is uncovered, because st-1.mjs probes History every 5 s from +20 s. Hosted runners have no cloud-file provider, and SF_DATALESS cannot be set without one (DERIVED; this job records the probe). The synthetic fixture is therefore defined as a kernel-blocking FIFO at every path a mostly-evicted cloud folder would present, in the representative-profile shape of ARCHITECTURE 6.1 (59 meetings, 6 cloud-only, a mostly cloud-only .brain), with History idle. MUST LAND BEFORE THE CUT: it edits qa-candidate.yml. st-1.mjs and qa-candidate.yml are in M2-0433's scope, so the two PRs are never open on these files at the same time. The preferred order is this ticket first (additive flags and one new job), with M2-0433 rebasing, so M2-0433's final self-test covers it. It is one of five before-cut PRs on qa-candidate.yml.
